text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Opposition parties walked out of Parliament Tuesday in protest against the rejection for the second time of their nomination of a law professor to the Constitutional Court. Parliament passed a bill on mortgage institutes and mortgage certificates, and amended a 1992 law on compensation for those deprived of life or freedom for political reasons.
- The Health Insurance Fund anticipates a 45 billion to 60 billion forints deficit instead of the projected 3.8 billion forints, said director general Agnes Cser.
- The Interest Coordination Council Tuesday agreed on a method for calculating annual increases in pensions.

- The disciplinary and ethics committee of the Christian Democratic Party yesterday declared that the mandate of party president Gyorgy Giczy and the governing board expired on January 27, and as no lawful elections have since been held, the party has no legitimate leadership.
- The Constitutional Court struck down a clause in the conflict of interest law alowing those MPs who held economic posts before entering Parliament to retain those posts.

- Slovenia will shortly open a consulate in Szentgotthard, according to an agreement between President Arpad Goncz and his Slovenian counterpart Milan Kucan. The two presidents also agreed on developing two border stations and construction additional TV relay stations.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs pledged Hungary's support for Romania's entry into NATO at a Tuesday meeting with Petre Roman, president of the Romanian Senate.

- EIB president Sir Brian Unwin and Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy Tuesday signed a statement of intent in Budapest on an ECU 120 million line of credit to the Hungarian state railway MAV for rail development.
- OTP Bank Rt.'s final 1996 report shows after-tax profit of 9.9 billion forints on pre-tax earnings of 13 billion forints.
- The Swedish-Swiss engineering group Asea Brown Boveri has purchased Dunaferr Rt's electrical machine repair plant for 170 million forints.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will pay an official visit to Copenhagen on May 2.
- Ten European and overseas foreign trade missions will be closed down before June 10.
- Malev is challenging the contract for the construction of a new passenger terminal at Ferihegy airport, claiming that the contract has several irregularities and is harmful to Hungarian interests.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- German Agriculture Minister Jochen Borchert arrived in Hungary on Tuesday for a two-day visit.
- BUX Index grew 103 points on Tuesday, closing a new high of 5,953 points.
- Richter Gedeon pharmaceutical company posted after-tax profits of 4.9 billion forints in the first quarter, 36 percent up on the same period of last year.
- Egis Rt. closed last year with after-tax profits of 5.6 billion forints on sales of 24.69 billion forints.
- Raiffeisen Unicbank posted pre-tax and pre-risk reserve profits of 1.7 billion forints in the first three months of this year.
- The Hungarian Electricity Works closed last year with losses of 12.9 billion forints on sales of 178.6 billion.
